raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Release FlashInfer one-sided all-to-all resources when vLLM destroys its expert-parallel communicator, while CUDA and the CPU process group are still alive.

## Claims

- `FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager.destroy()` now releases its communicator instead of inheriting a no-op.
- With the pinned FlashInfer 0.7.2, remove the owned legacy workspace cache reference so symmetric allocations do not survive until Python finalization. Preserve references held by other live wrappers.

## Validation

Validated on two GB200 GPUs with PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 and FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing lifecycle worker, extended to call `destroy()` | Fails `not manager.initialized`; worker finalization also segfaults | Passes, including cache eviction, reinitialization, and repeated destruction |
| Existing workspace-growth worker | — | Passes |
| Existing BF16 dispatch/combine worker | — | Passes |
| Native `vllm bench forward`, tiny Qwen3 MoE BF16, DP2/EP2, FlashInfer CUTLASS and one-sided A2A | — | Prefill and decode finish with finite, deterministic outputs and graph/eager RMS 0 on both ranks; clean process exit |

The real distributed workers were invoked directly because this host's pytest capability marker skips the tests without `SYS_PTRACE`; its CUDA FABRIC allocation path works. No communicator or allocation was mocked. The existing B200 distributed CI step runs these tests in its supported environment.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -c 'from tests.distributed.test_mnnvl_alltoall import _spawn_workers, _one_sided_lifecycle_worker; _spawn_workers(_one_sided_lifecycle_worker, 2, dp_size=2)'
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -c 'from tests.distributed.test_mnnvl_alltoall import _spawn_workers, _one_sided_workspace_grow_worker; _spawn_workers(_one_sided_workspace_grow_worker, 2, dp_size=2)'
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -c 'from functools import partial; from tests.distributed.test_mnnvl_alltoall import _spawn_workers, _one_sided_data_worker; _spawn_workers(partial(_one_sided_data_worker, padded_mxfp8=False), 2, dp_size=2)'
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py docs/design/moe_kernel_features.md
```

All targeted pre-commit hooks pass. This changes resource lifetime, not model arithmetic; no quality or performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

The existing group teardown already calls the CUDA communicator's `destroy()` before destroying process groups. The one-sided manager lacked an override, and its explicit `cleanup()` only destroyed FlashInfer's wrapper. In FlashInfer 0.7.2 that leaves the symmetric workspace in a process-wide cache, which can release CUDA tensors too late during interpreter finalization.

Cleanup now synchronizes outstanding device work and ranks before destroying the wrapper and removing only cache entries that refer to that workspace. It does not clear or mutate the workspace itself, so other wrappers keep their own references. The same cleanup handles workspace growth before graph capture. Newer FlashInfer implementations without the legacy wrapper use their public `destroy()` directly. No synchronization is added to steady-state dispatch/combine.

Duplicate checks found no open PR with this lifecycle fix. The current diff of [#47733](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47733) changes invalid expert IDs and scaling in prepare/finalize; despite its older body mentioning destruction, it does not add this manager teardown. FlashInfer main has a newer workspace lifecycle, but vLLM currently pins the affected released version.

AI assistance was used to implement, test, and review this change. The human submitter confirmed review of every changed line and execution of the relevant tests before submission.

---

files.patch:
@@ -54,6 +54,13 @@ th {
     - A - Per activation token
     - T - Per tensor
 
+`flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` releases its communication workspace during
+expert-parallel group teardown, before the process groups are destroyed.
+This also releases the manager's legacy process-wide workspace cache entries
+when using FlashInfer 0.7.2, so they do not survive until Python finalization.
+Custom integrations must finish outstanding GPU work and destroy the manager
+collectively while its CPU process group is still available.
+
 Modular kernels are supported by the following `FusedMoEMethodBase` classes.
 
 - [`ModelOptFp8MoEMethod`][vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.modelopt.ModelOptFp8MoEMethod]

@@ -351,13 +351,18 @@ def _one_sided_lifecycle_worker(rank, world_size):
         assert torch.get_default_device() == torch.device(f"{DEVICE}:{rank}")
     assert manager.initialized
     assert manager.get_communication().params.hidden_size == 4096
+    legacy = getattr(manager.get_communication(), "alltoall", None)
+    workspace_id = id(getattr(legacy, "_WORKSPACE", None))
+    workspace_cache = getattr(type(legacy), "_WORKSPACE_CACHE", {})
+    del legacy
 
     torch.distributed.barrier()
 
-    # Cleanup
-    manager.cleanup()
+    # Group teardown calls destroy(), while layer setup can call cleanup().
+    manager.destroy()
     assert not manager.initialized
     assert manager.communication is None
+    assert all(id(value) != workspace_id for value in workspace_cache.values())
 
     torch.distributed.barrier()
 
@@ -366,15 +371,18 @@ def _one_sided_lifecycle_worker(rank, world_size):
     assert manager.initialized
 
     torch.distributed.barrier()
-    manager.cleanup()
+    manager.destroy()
+    manager.destroy()
+    assert not manager.initialized
+    assert manager.communication is None
 
 
 @requires_multi_gpu
 @requires_one_sided
 @requires_ptrace
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("world_size", [2])
 def test_one_sided_manager_lifecycle(world_size):
-    """Test init, cleanup, and reinit with different params."""
+    """Destroy releases the communicator/cache before process-group teardown."""
     _spawn_workers(
         _one_sided_lifecycle_worker,
         world_size,

@@ -857,10 +857,6 @@ def initialize(
         )
         if communication is not None:
             # Growth happens during model initialization, before graph capture.
-            # Destroy the old wrapper on every rank before replacing it;
-            # FlashInfer owns the underlying workspace cache.
-            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
-            dist.barrier(group=self.cpu_group)
             self.cleanup()
             dist.barrier(group=self.cpu_group)
         torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
@@ -892,10 +888,25 @@ def get_handle(self, kwargs):
 
     def cleanup(self):
         if self.communication is not None:
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+            dist.barrier(group=self.cpu_group)
+            # FlashInfer 0.7.2 keeps the legacy workspace alive after destroy().
+            # Evict only this cache entry; other live wrappers retain their
+            # own references until they are destroyed.
+            legacy = getattr(self.communication, "alltoall", None)
+            workspace = getattr(legacy, "_WORKSPACE", None)
+            cache = getattr(type(legacy), "_WORKSPACE_CACHE", {})
             self.communication.destroy()
             self.communication = None
+            if workspace is not None:
+                for key, value in list(cache.items()):
+                    if value is workspace:
+                        del cache[key]
         self.initialized = False
 
+    def destroy(self):
+        self.cleanup()
+
     def checkpoint_prepare(self) -> None:
         if self.communication is not None:
             communication = self.communication
